name: mcuctl
description: Connect to MicroPython and CircuitPython boards over USB serial or Wi-Fi (WebREPL): dual-pane file transfer, ANSI REPL, mip/circup packages, and guided MicroPython firmware download/build/flash. Works on Linux, Windows, and WSL (COM ports via Windows Python).

MCU Control: Forget a Wi-Fi Board…

mcuctl.pythonPath.description: Python 3.9+ for the serial sidecar (mpremote and pyserial are bundled; circup for CircuitPython packages and esptool for flashing come from this interpreter). On WSL, leave empty to auto-use Windows python.exe so COM ports work.

mcuctl.mpremotePath.description: Optional path to mpremote / mpremote.exe (used for port listing fallback and diagnostics).

mcuctl.autoConnectDevice.description: Auto-connect device path (e.g. COM4 or /dev/ttyACM0). Empty disables auto-connect.

mcuctl.verifyTransfers.description: After each file upload/download, verify with SHA-256 against the board.

mcuctl.compileOnUpload.description: Compile .py files to .mpy via mpy-cross before uploading (MicroPython only; boot.py/main.py are never compiled). Requires mpy-cross in the firmware workspace or on PATH.

mcuctl.autoReconnectAfterReset.description: After hard reset, wait for the same COM port and reconnect automatically.

mcuctl.openEditorOnConnect.description: When a board connects, open File Transfer as an editor tab and the REPL terminal (skipped for silent reconnects).

mcuctl.workspacePath.description: Firmware workspace: the folder where mcuctl looks for an omnipython-builds checkout (whose build_mp.py builds firmware) and a MicroPython tree.

mcuctl.buildSystemPath.description: The omnipython-builds checkout the Firmware panel builds with (the folder holding build_mp.py). Set, it wins over every other way of finding one; a folder that isn't a checkout is an error, not a fallback. Leave empty to use buildSystemPath from ~/.mcuctl/config.json (or MCUCTL_BUILD_SYSTEM), then the firmware workspace and open folders, then a folder beside the MicroPython tree, then ~/omnipython-builds.

mcuctl.micropythonPath.description: Override path to the MicroPython checkout (ports/ + py/). Leave empty to resolve from the firmware workspace, MP_DIR, or ~/micropython.

mcuctl.idfPath.description: Override path to ESP-IDF (export.sh). Leave empty to use IDF_PATH / IDF_DIR or an esp-idf directory/symlink under the firmware workspace.

mcuctl.emsdkPath.description: Override path to emsdk (emsdk_env.sh). Leave empty to use EMSDK / EMSDK_DIR or an emsdk directory/symlink under the firmware workspace.

mcuctl.toolchainBins.description: Extra cross-toolchain bin/ folders prepended to the build PATH (e.g. arm-none-eabi, xtensa, riscv, xc16, mingw-w64). Populated when you locate a missing toolchain from the build prompt; edit here to add more.

mcuctl.buildPythonPath.description: Python used to run the firmware build engine and make. On WSL this must be a native Linux python3. Leave empty to auto-detect.

mcuctl.esptoolCommand.description: Override the esptool command used to flash esp32 (e.g. a Windows python.exe on WSL so it can see COM ports). Leave empty to auto-detect.

enumDescriptions: Ask once per board whether the CLI, the PWA and agents may use its password
Also save every board's password in ~/.mcuctl/webrepl-passwords.json
Keep passwords in VS Code's secret storage only
mcuctl.sharePasswords.markdownDescription: Where a WebREPL or bledev password you type in VS Code is kept. It always goes in VS Code's secret storage. The mcuctl command line, the PWA and agents read `~/.mcuctl/webrepl-passwords.json` instead (plaintext, readable only by you), so a password shared there works from all of them. VS Code reads that file too, so a password saved by the CLI or the PWA works here without asking.
